blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A water utility has promised its regulator to replace a minimum of 40 km of lead pipe this year, and within that promise it wants the cheapest plan. Which model asks exactly that?

options.text: Maximize km replaced, subject to km replaced of at least 40 and every rule
options.says: This asks for the most km; the promise needs only 40 km, and the wish is about cost.

options.text: Minimize total cost, subject to km replaced of at least 40 and every rule
options.says: Right: the commitment becomes the floor, and what the utility wants as little of as possible stays the objective.

options.text: Minimize total cost minus 40 times km replaced, subject to every rule
options.says: That is a weighted sum: it needs a price for a km and promises no 40 km at all.

options.text: Minimize total cost, subject to km replaced of at most 40 and every rule
options.says: At most 40 km caps the promise instead of meeting it; the promise is a minimum.

origin.section: Keep One Objective, and Turn the Other Into a Floor

questions.stem: A payoff table has two plans. Plan A, best on value, scores (value 900, safety 40); plan B, best on safety, scores (value 600, safety 75). A planner maximizes value with a safety floor of 30, then again with a floor of 80. What comes back?

options.text: Floor 30 returns no plan at all, and floor 80 returns plan B
options.says: A floor below the range does nothing: plan A already clears 30 and has the most value.

options.text: Floor 30 returns a plan between A and B, and floor 80 returns plan B
options.says: A floor below plan A's safety does not bind, so the answer is plan A itself; and no plan reaches 80.

options.text: Floor 30 returns plan B, and floor 80 returns plan B as well
options.says: Plan B has less value than A, and A meets the floor of 30; 80 is above any plan's safety.

options.text: Floor 30 returns plan A, and floor 80 returns no plan at all
options.says: Right: below the range the floor does nothing, and above the best safety in the table no plan exists.

origin.section: The Payoff Table Sets the Range of ε

questions.stem: A colleague sweeps 10 evenly spaced floors over the payoff table's range, gets 9 different plans, and writes: "the frontier has 9 Pareto plans". What should the review say?

options.text: Correct, since a sweep of floors returns each plan on the frontier
options.says: Each floor returns one plan; plans whose interval holds no floor are never returned.

options.text: Wrong, since the frontier has one plan per floor, so 10
options.says: The frontier depends on the data, not on the grid; two floors can return the same plan.

options.text: Unproven, since plans can sit between floors the grid skipped
options.says: Right: a grid finds every plan only when its step is finer than the gap between neighbouring plans.

options.text: Correct, since a repeated plan means the sweep has passed the last plan
options.says: A repeat means two floors fell between the same neighbours, as 21 floors giving 20 plans showed.

origin.section: A Sweep Finds at Most One Plan per Floor, So Its Steps Must Fit the Data
